title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1RC---_0RD0RE_1LE0RF_0LA0LD_1RD0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1RC---_0RD0RE_1LE0RF_0LA0LD_1RD0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. This page describes what its run looks like at the level of words and counters, what a halt would need, and what is still missing. The description comes from simulation (first look, about an hour of study); nothing beyond the bounded runs is proved.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps, the C simulator none in 109. The macro structure described below is observed in the simulation, not proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 127,559 cells have been visited and 124,373 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.659).

claims.title: Working counter
claims.text: At the D-right samples the end of the tape is 1^u 0 (10)^v 1 with u + v constant over a stretch of samples (u = 4,699 to 199 while v = 6,110 to 10,610).

claims.title: Stack of records
claims.text: Left of the working part are records 1^s 0 (10)^k 1 0^2 left by earlier epochs, some of which are later rebuilt.

claims.title: The working-counter cycles, for every length
claims.text: cycA: L (11)^(n+1) (01)^(p+1) D> → L (11)^n (01)^(p+3) D>; cycB: L (11)^(n+2) (01)^(p+1) 0010 (01)^(q+1) D> → L (11)^n (01)^(p+3) 0010 (01)^(q+2) D>; for any tape L.

claims.title: Those cycles cover 99.55% of the run
claims.text: With the cycle accelerator (block size 2), 0.9955 of the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps lie inside jumps of these two shapes (35 jumps over 24,712 cycles of the first shape, 72 over 38,028 of the second, the one with the marker).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No macro rule has been proved for this machine yet; see the README's Later section for the next steps.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. A working counter at the right end turns a block of 1s into 10 pairs; when it runs out it reads the record below it, so the tape becomes a growing stack of records.

facts.text: the tape grows to the right about like t^0.66
No halt in the C simulator; 127,559 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A working counter on a stack of records
html: Write a for the pair 1 0. Each time the head is at the right end in state D, the end of the tape reads like … 1^6903 0 a^13 1 0^2 1^5 0 a^2 1 0^2 1^4699 0 a^6110 1 D>1 (step 266,560,790): a working part 1^u 0 a^v 1 in which u falls and v rises by the same amount (u = 4,699, 3,199, 1,699, 199 and v = 6,110, 7,610, 9,110, 10,610 at four samples 1,500 apart), and to its left records 1^s 0 a^k 1 0^2 left by earlier epochs.

When u runs out the working part is rebuilt from the record below it, so the records act as a stack that is popped and pushed. The far left of the tape is frozen (1^8 0 a^5 1 0^2 1^25 0 a 1 0^2 …). The tape grows to the right like t0.66.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine halts when it reads a 1 in state B (B1 is the halting transition). B is entered from A on a 0 (A0 = 1RB) and from F on a 1 (F1 = 0RB), so a halt needs A>0 1 or F>1 1.

sections.heading: The counter cycles proved
html: The working part of the counter runs by two cycles proved for every length: (11)^(n+1) (01)^(p+1) D> turns one 11 into two 01, and the variant with a 0010 marker turns two 11 into three 01. Together they cover 99.55% of the first 109 steps. What is left is what happens when a counter runs out and the next record is read; that map (the record stack) is not found yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.659).
After 109 steps the tape spans 127,559 cells (10 left of the start, 82,720 right), with a density of 1s of 0.975.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: counter epochs at the right end leaving a stack of records
summary: Activity happens at the right end, where a block 1^u is converted into 10 pairs and back; each epoch leaves a record of blocks behind, so the tape is a growing stack of frozen records with a working counter on top.
